title: Does Norfolk prevent litter, or only pick it up?
summary: As of November 23, 2026: Norfolk and Keep Norfolk Beautiful (KNB, part of Public Works) run some prevention (education, free cigarette receptacles, litter tracking in the International Coastal Cleanup, a state litter-prevention grant, and the 2022 Litterati study meant to test prevention on commercial corridors), but most of what KNB’s Reduce Litter page offers residents is cleanup: pop-up cleanups, Adopt-a-Spot, the Green Bucket Brigade and annual cleanup events. The state grant is DEQ’s non-competitive Litter Prevention and Recycling Grant, awarded to localities that apply and meet DEQ’s eligibility requirements: the adopted Annual Grants Plans listed up to $60,000 for KNB in FY 2024 (Council added up to $69,257.93 in January 2024), $100,000 for FY 2025 and $80,000 for FY 2026; the much smaller FY 2027 plan doesn’t name KNB or any Public Works grant, and no FY 2027 award or ordinance was found. No results of the 2022 prevention test were found, Norfolk is still not among the localities with Virginia’s 5-cent bag tax, and no record was found of enforcing the state rule requiring litter receptacles at gas stations, fast-food restaurants and shopping centers.

what_would_help.text: Adopt Virginia's 5-cent bag tax; its revenue is earmarked for litter and pollution work.
Enforce the state receptacle rule at gas stations, fast-food restaurants and shopping centers on the hotspot corridors.
Put serviced cigarette receptacles at business entrances and the busiest bus stops, and measure butt counts before and after.
Publish the results of the 2022 Litterati prevention study and resume the Litter Index, last published for 2019.
Keep applying for DEQ's non-competitive litter grant each year and list it in the Annual Grants Plan, so residents can see what prevention it pays for.

records_to_request: The Litterati City Fingerprint final report, contract and cost, and the interventions tested, with dates and places.
Keep Norfolk Beautiful's budget and staffing, FY2020 to now, and DEQ litter-prevention grant applications and reports.
How many free cigarette receptacles were given out, and where.
Any enforcement of 9VAC20-190, and littering, dumping and uncovered-load summonses since 2020, by location.
Any staff analysis or council briefing on the bag tax (Va. Code 58.1-1745).

Norfolk's applications to DEQ for the non-competitive Litter Prevention and Recycling Grant for grant years 2025, 2026 and 2027, DEQ's award letters, and the year-end reports on how the money was spent.
Keep Norfolk Beautiful's cleanup totals (pop-up, Adopt-a-Spot, Green Bucket Brigade and International Coastal Cleanup tracking sheets) since 2022.
pending: Keep Norfolk Beautiful’s DEQ grant line in the FY2020 and FY2021 Annual Grants Plans ($35,000, per the original researcher); not yet re-checked. FY2024 ($60,000), FY2025 ($100,000) and FY2026 ($80,000) are now findings.

Whether Norfolk applied for and received DEQ's non-competitive litter grant for FY 2027 (grant year 2027): the FY 2027 Annual Grants Plan doesn't list it, Siren's legislation index has no acceptance ordinance after January 2024, and DEQ's grant pages refused this environment's requests.

The City's Litter Prevention page (norfolk.gov/5256) still advertises an International Coastal Cleanup "20th anniversary" focus day on Saturday, October 17, which looks years out of date; not used for findings.
The grants plans name the line "Keep Norfolk Beautiful" from DEQ, not the "Litter Prevention and Recycling Grant"; reading them as the same grant is an inference from Ordinance 49464.
